description: Fix three blocking WiFi provisioning bugs (scan finds nothing, block char in label, captive portal crash) and harden the full AP -> portal -> connect -> STA flow for reliable field demos. WiFi chip is ESP32-C6.

userStories.title: Fix WiFi mode so scanning works in AP+STA coexistence
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the ESP32 WiFi mode set to WIFI_MODE_APSTA before scanning so that esp_wifi_scan_start() can find networks while the soft-AP is active.
acceptanceCriteria: wifi_manager_start_ap() calls esp_wifi_set_mode(WIFI_MODE_APSTA) instead of WIFI_MODE_AP
wifi_manager_scan() (wifi_manager.c:232) is only called after the AP is started so mode is already APSTA
WIFI_EVENT_SCAN_DONE fires and scan_done_cb() receives at least one AP entry when a real network is in range
If scan returns zero APs, scan_done_cb() shows 'No networks found' in the status label instead of an empty list
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/wifi_manager.c produces zero errors
Typecheck passes
Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: tapping Scan on the WiFi setup screen populates a list of nearby networks
userStories.notes: WiFi chip is ESP32-C6. WIFI_MODE_APSTA coexistence is supported on C6 with ESP-IDF 5.x.

userStories.title: Replace U+2026 ellipsis with ASCII fallback in scan label
userStories.description: As a user, I want the Scanning... label to display clean text so the UI looks professional during provisioning.
acceptanceCriteria: ui_wifi_setup.c:172 uses "Scanning..." (three ASCII full stops, no UTF-8 escape \xe2\x80\xa6)
Search entire main/ui/ directory for any other \xe2\x80\xa6 occurrences and replace all with ...
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/ui/ui_wifi_setup.c produces zero errors
Typecheck passes
Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: no block character (□) appears on the scan screen during or after scanning

userStories.title: Increase HTTP server task stack to prevent portal crash
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the captive portal HTTP server task to have enough stack so it does not crash when serving the scan-results HTML page.
acceptanceCriteria: wifi_portal.c sets config.stack_size = 8192 on the httpd_config_t before httpd_start()
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/wifi_portal.c produces zero errors
Typecheck passes
Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: iPhone can navigate to http://192.168.4.1/ and sees the HTML provisioning form without the device rebooting

userStories.title: Move blocking scan out of HTTP handler into pre-cached background scan
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the root HTTP handler to serve a pre-cached scan result instead of blocking the server task with a synchronous scan so we eliminate the stack-depth risk permanently.
acceptanceCriteria: wifi_portal_start() calls wifi_manager_scan() immediately after the AP starts to pre-populate the cache
A module-level s_cached_aps[] array (max WIFI_SCAN_MAX entries) and s_cached_ap_count counter are added to wifi_portal.c
A portal_scan_done_cb() callback populates s_cached_aps[] and s_cached_ap_count; registered with wifi_manager_scan()
get_root_handler() reads from s_cached_aps[] only; it does not call esp_wifi_scan_start() directly
If s_cached_ap_count == 0 (scan not yet complete), get_root_handler() serves the form with a 'Scanning, please refresh' notice instead of an empty dropdown
A GET /rescan URI handler is registered before the GET /* wildcard; it calls wifi_manager_scan() and redirects to /
HTTP server task stack size remains 8192 (set in US-003)
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/wifi_portal.c produces zero errors
Typecheck passes
Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: portal form shows a populated network dropdown; submitting correct credentials causes the device to connect and iPhone sees a success page

userStories.title: Add DNS hijack so iOS redirects to portal automatically
userStories.description: As a user, I want the captive portal to open automatically when I connect to the SAP-DM-Setup hotspot so I do not need to manually type 192.168.4.1.
acceptanceCriteria: A minimal UDP DNS responder task is implemented (port 53, answers all A-record queries with 192.168.4.1)
DNS responder task is started inside wifi_portal_start() after httpd_start()
DNS responder task is stopped and deleted inside wifi_portal_stop()
DNS responder task stack is at least 4096 bytes
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/wifi_portal.c (or new dns_responder.c if extracted) produces zero errors
Typecheck passes
Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: iOS auto-opens the captive portal UI within ~5 seconds of joining the SAP-DM-Setup network without manually typing the IP
userStories.notes: ESP32-C6 uses lwIP for networking; standard BSD socket API (recvfrom/sendto on SOCK_DGRAM port 53) works fine.

userStories.title: Show provisioning status on device display during portal flow
userStories.description: As a demo operator, I want the device screen to reflect the portal state so I can confirm what is happening without a serial monitor.
acceptanceCriteria: wifi_portal_start() fires an lv_async_call to set the WiFi setup screen status label to 'Hotspot active - connect to SAP-DM-Setup'
On STA association event (phone joins AP), status label updates to 'Phone connected' via lv_async_call
On POST /connect received, status label updates to 'Connecting to [SSID]...' via lv_async_call
On successful STA connection (IP_EVENT_STA_GOT_IP), status label updates to 'Connected!' via lv_async_call and navigates to the main screen after 2 seconds
On failed STA connection (WIFI_EVENT_STA_DISCONNECTED with non-zero reason), status label updates to 'Connection failed - try again' via lv_async_call
No direct LVGL API calls from event handlers or HTTP task (all go through lv_async_call)
Direct riscv32-esp-elf-gcc compile of main/wifi_portal.c and main/ui/ui_wifi_setup.c produces zero errors
Typecheck passes

Flash to device using idf.py flash and human-verify: device screen progresses through 'Hotspot active' -> 'Phone connected' -> 'Connecting to [SSID]...' -> 'Connected!' during a full provisioning flow without a serial monitor
